# `silk/concurrency/atomic`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Atomic memory operations on raw pointers, with explicit memory orderings.

## When to use
Use these operations to build synchronization: counters, flags, lock words, and queues that
several threads read and write at the same time. For most code, the types in `silk.concurrency.sync` (`Arc`,
`Mutex`, `Parker`) are easier and safer.

## Details
Each operation is one indivisible access to a naturally aligned integer or data pointer. The
[`MemoryOrder`](#MemoryOrder) argument is static, so the operation and its ordering are fixed at compile time.
The model is the C++20 model: an acquire load that reads a release store makes every write
before that store visible after the load.

[`Atomic.wait`](#Atomic.impl.wait), [`Atomic.notifyOne`](#Atomic.impl.notifyOne) and [`Atomic.notifyAll`](#Atomic.impl.notifyAll) are a futex: a thread sleeps
until the value at an address changes. They work on Darwin on x86_64 or aarch64, Linux with GNU libc on
x86_64 or aarch64, and wasm32.

## Gotchas
- A plain access that races with any other access to the same location is undefined behavior,
  also when the other access is atomic. Make every access to a shared location atomic, with the
  same width.
- All operations except [`Atomic.fence`](#Atomic.impl.fence) are unsafe. The caller proves that the pointer is live
  and aligned.

## Examples
### Count and claim a flag
```silk
import silk.concurrency.atomic { Atomic, CompareExchange, MemoryOrder }
import silk.mem.pointer { Pointer }

// Claims a one-time flag. Only the first caller gets true.
fn claim(flag: *mut u32) -> bool {
  return match unsafe Atomic.compareExchange<u32>(
    flag,
    0,
    1,
    MemoryOrder.Acquire,
    MemoryOrder.Relaxed
  ) {
    CompareExchange<u32>.Exchanged => true
    CompareExchange<u32>.Observed { value } => false
  }
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut hits: u64 = 0
  let counter = Pointer.fromMutRef(&mut hits)

  // fetchAdd returns the value before the add.
  let before = unsafe Atomic.fetchAdd<u64>(counter, 5, MemoryOrder.Relaxed)
  if before != 0 || unsafe Atomic.load<u64>(counter, MemoryOrder.Relaxed) != 5 {
    return 1
  }

  let mut claimed: u32 = 0
  let flag = Pointer.fromMutRef(&mut claimed)
  if !claim(flag) || claim(flag) {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

## `MemoryOrder`

```silk
pub enum MemoryOrder
```

The ordering constraint of one atomic operation.

### Details

The model is the C++20 model: an acquire load that reads a release store makes every write
before that store visible after the load. The order is a static argument, so the operation and
its ordering are fixed at compile time.

<a id="MemoryOrder.Relaxed"></a>

### `Relaxed`

```silk
Relaxed
```

Atomicity only. It orders no other access.

<a id="MemoryOrder.Acquire"></a>

### `Acquire`

```silk
Acquire
```

A load that later reads and writes cannot move before.

<a id="MemoryOrder.Release"></a>

### `Release`

```silk
Release
```

A store that earlier reads and writes cannot move after.

<a id="MemoryOrder.AcquireRelease"></a>

### `AcquireRelease`

```silk
AcquireRelease
```

Both acquire and release. Use it for read-modify-write operations and fences.

<a id="MemoryOrder.SequentiallyConsistent"></a>

### `SequentiallyConsistent`

```silk
SequentiallyConsistent
```

Acquire and release, plus one total order over every sequentially consistent operation.

<a id="Atomic"></a>

## `Atomic`

```silk
pub struct Atomic
```

The atomic operations over raw pointers, with explicit memory orderings.

### When to use

Use these operations to build synchronization: counters, flags, lock words, and queues that
several threads read and write at the same time. For most code, the types in `silk.concurrency.sync` (`Arc`,
`Mutex`, `Parker`) are easier and safer.

### Details

Each operation is one indivisible access to a naturally aligned integer or data pointer.
`T` is one of `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `usize`, `i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `isize`, or a data
pointer for `load`, `store`, `swap`, and the compare-exchanges. The arithmetic and bitwise
operations take integers only and wrap on overflow.

### Gotchas

- A plain access that races with any other access to the same location is undefined behavior,
  also when the other access is atomic. Make every access to a shared location atomic, with the
  same width.
- All operations except [`Atomic.fence`](#Atomic.impl.fence) are unsafe. The caller proves that the pointer is live
  and aligned.

<a id="Atomic.impl.load"></a>

### Associated function `load`

```silk
pub unsafe fn load<T: Copy>(pointer: *const T, static order: MemoryOrder) -> T
```

Reads the pointee atomically.

#### Safety

The pointer must address live, initialized, naturally aligned storage for `T`. The order must
be `Relaxed`, `Acquire`, or `SequentiallyConsistent`.
Every access to the same location that can happen at the same time must be atomic and have
the same width.

<a id="Atomic.impl.compareExchange"></a>

### Associated function `compareExchange`

```silk
pub unsafe fn compareExchange<T: Copy>(pointer: *mut T, expected: T, desired: T, static success: MemoryOrder,
    static failure: MemoryOrder) -> CompareExchange<T>
```

Stores `desired` if the pointee equals `expected`. Otherwise it returns the value it read.

#### Details
`success` orders the exchange. `failure` orders the read when nothing is stored. `failure`
must be `Relaxed`, `Acquire`, or `SequentiallyConsistent`.

#### Safety
The pointer must address live, initialized, naturally aligned, writable storage for `T`.
Every access to the same location that can happen at the same time must be atomic and have
the same width.

<a id="Atomic.impl.compareExchangeWeak"></a>

### Associated function `compareExchangeWeak`

```silk
pub unsafe fn compareExchangeWeak<T: Copy>(pointer: *mut T, expected: T, desired: T, static success: MemoryOrder,
    static failure: MemoryOrder) -> CompareExchange<T>
```

Stores `desired` if the pointee equals `expected`. Otherwise it returns the value it read. It
can also fail spuriously: return `Observed` with a value equal to `expected`.

#### When to use
Use it in a retry loop. Use [`Atomic.compareExchange`](#Atomic.impl.compareExchange) when one attempt must decide.

#### Details
This spurious failure lets a load-linked, store-conditional target use one attempt per call.
Call it in a loop that retries on any observed value. `success` orders the exchange. `failure`
orders the read when nothing is stored. `failure` must be `Relaxed`, `Acquire`, or
`SequentiallyConsistent`.

#### Safety
The pointer must address live, initialized, naturally aligned, writable storage for `T`.
Every access to the same location that can happen at the same time must be atomic and have
the same width.

<a id="Atomic.impl.wait"></a>

### Associated function `wait`

```silk
pub unsafe fn wait(pointer: *const u32, expected: u32, timeout: Option<u64>) -> bool
```

Sleeps while the pointee equals `expected`, until a notify, the timeout, or a spurious wakeup.

#### Details
The comparison and the sleep are one atomic step against [`Atomic.notifyOne`](#Atomic.impl.notifyOne) and
[`Atomic.notifyAll`](#Atomic.impl.notifyAll). Thus a notify after a store that changed the pointee is never lost.

`timeout` is a relative bound in nanoseconds. `Option.None` waits with no bound. The result is
`false` only when the timeout ended the wait. A `true` result tells nothing about the pointee,
so check the condition again in a loop.

It works on Windows x86_64 MSVC, Darwin on x86_64 or aarch64, Linux with GNU libc on x86_64 or aarch64, and wasm32.
Windows rounds finite bounds up to milliseconds. A bound above the largest finite Windows
wait is clamped; its expiry is a spurious wakeup, not a reported timeout.

#### Gotchas
Single-threaded WebAssembly has no other thread to change the pointee. A wait that sleeps with
no timeout traps, and a wait with a timeout returns `false` at once.

#### Safety
The pointer must address live, naturally aligned storage for a `u32`. Every other access to it
must be atomic.

<a id="Atomic.impl.notifyOne"></a>

### Associated function `notifyOne`

```silk
pub unsafe fn notifyOne(pointer: *const u32) -> ()
```

Wakes at least one thread blocked in [`Atomic.wait`](#Atomic.impl.wait) on `pointer`, if any is.

#### Details

Store the new value before the notify. A waiter that has not yet slept sees the changed value
and does not sleep, so the wakeup is never lost. It works on Windows x86_64 MSVC, Darwin on x86_64 or aarch64, Linux with GNU
libc on x86_64 or aarch64, and wasm32.

#### Safety

The pointer must address live, naturally aligned storage for a `u32`.

Store the new value before the notify. A waiter that has not yet slept sees the changed value
and does not sleep, so the wakeup is never lost. It works on Windows x86_64 MSVC, Darwin on x86_64 or aarch64, Linux with GNU
libc on x86_64 or aarch64, and wasm32.

#### Safety

The pointer must address live, naturally aligned storage for a `u32`.

<a id="Atomic.impl.fence"></a>

### Associated function `fence`

```silk
pub fn fence(static order: MemoryOrder) -> ()
```

Orders memory accesses around this point without accessing memory itself.

#### Details

The order must not be `Relaxed`. A release fence before a relaxed store, paired with an
acquire fence after a relaxed load that reads it, synchronizes like a release store and an
acquire load.
